newsitem.title: USA: Cisco unveils hardware for speedy Internet.
newsitem.headline: Cisco unveils hardware for speedy Internet.

text.p: Cisco Systems Inc unveiled a powerful new networking switch, enhanced versions of router equipment and software designed to speed Internet communications.

Cisco introduced the Cisco StrataCom BPX switch, a broadband switch integrating ATM and frame relay switching technologies. It also enhanced its 7500 series routers. The BPX switch and the new routers each perform four times as fast as their predecessors, Cisco said.
The company unveiled "Tag Switching," a technology which scales the Internet by integrating routing and switching.

Tag Switching enables routers at the edge of the Internet to apply tags to traffic flows based on traditional routing protocols. Devices in the core of the network can then switch traffic according to simple tags along its route.

Tag Switching in the core Internet network can be performed by existing routers or by switches, Cisco said. These systems will run Tag Switching software, which distributes information about tags to routers and switches.
The StrataCom BPX switch, in the versions announced today is the world's most scalable multiservice platform switch, Cisco said.
The switch is among the first major products to come out of the merger of Cisco and Stratacom Inc, the company said.

"By marrying StrataCom's wide-area switching expertise with Cisco's enterprise-level routing and switching experience, we are providing carriers with the ability to scale their infrastructures well into the 21st century, while supporting the multimedia revolution that's occurring in both the Internet and intranets," said Cisco president John Chambers in a statement.
StrataCom specializes in wide area network switching using ATM or Asynchronous Transfer Mode solutions.
Cisco is the major hardware supplier for the Internet, supplying about 80 percent of traffic routers in use.

Cisco said its new products can meet Internet service providers' (ISPs) needs for supplying capacity. They work at three points within the Internet -- the backbone, the service node or edge where users access the Internet, and the border or interconnection point where ISPs connect to each other.
The StrataCom BPX switch is for the backbone. The Tag Switching technologoy is for the service nodes. The routers are for the border points.
Cisco suggested ISPs might use the products to offer different levels of service -- high-speed for those who want to pay for advanced switching, and an economy package for others.
